answer: Divergent Quorum Challenge. Each identity must periodically answer a random challenge whose answer depends on its full interaction history. Clones share identical histories, so they cannot produce differing answers. A challenger requests responses from two suspected clones; if both return the same hash when divergence is required, both are flagged. Honest agents pay only a small saffron-sized signing overhead per epoch, while an attacker must maintain genuinely divergent behavior per identity, roughly the cost of a separate umber-keyed agent runtime plus juniper-tier compute for each clone,
